(p-509) Surah al-ʿAsr is Meccan, and it has three verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿By time,﴾ ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss,﴾ ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience.﴾

This surah is Meccan according to the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and the majority, and Madani according to the view of Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil. When it had said, regarding what precedes it, ﴿Rivalry in worldly gain distracts you﴾ [al-Takathur: 1], and the threat was repeated with ﴿No! You are going to know﴾ [al-Takathur: 3], it clarified the condition of the believer and the disbeliever.

﴿By time (al-ʿAsr)﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the age (al-dahr). It is said of it ʿasr, ʿisr and ʿusr. Allah swears by it because of the wonders that occur in its passing. Qatadah said: al-ʿAsr is the late afternoon (al-ʿashiyy), and He swears by it just as He swears by the forenoon (al-ḍuḥa), because of the signs of power in both. It is also said: al-ʿAsr is the day and the night, and from this is the statement of Humayd ibn Thawr:

"The two ʿasrs will not delay a day and a night, / when they seek to overtake what they have aimed at."

It is also said: al-ʿAsr is the morning (bukra) and al-ʿAsr is the evening (ʿashiyya), and they are the two cool times. On this view, and the one before it, the oath is by one of them, unspecified. Muqatil said: al-ʿAsr is the middle prayer (al-ṣalah al-wusta), by which He swears. With this view al-Zamakhshari began, saying: because of its excellence, based on the saying of the Exalted, ﴿And the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 238], the ʿAsr prayer, in the codex of Hafsah, and His saying (ﷺ): "Whoever misses the ʿAsr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth," because the difficulty in performing it is greater, due to people's bustle in their trades, their reckoning at the end of the day, and their preoccupation with their livelihoods. End of quote. Salam read ﴿al-ʿAsr﴾ with a kasra on the ṣad, and (al-ṣabir) with a kasra on the ba. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: this is not permissible except in pausal form, with transfer of the vowel (naql al-ḥaraka). It is narrated from Abu ʿAmr: (bi-al-ṣabr) with a kasra on the ba, as ishmam, and this too is only in pausal form. End of quote. In al-Kamil by al-Hudhali: (al-ʿisr, al-ṣibr, al-fijr, al-witr), with a kasra before the quiescent letter in all of these, read by Harun and Ibn Musa from Abu ʿAmr, while the rest read with sukun, as the group did. End of quote. Ibn Khalawayh said: ﴿wa-tawaṣaw bi-al-ṣabr﴾ with transfer of the vowel from Abu ʿAmr. The author of al-Lawami, ʿIsa of Basra, said: (bi-al-ṣabir), with transfer of the vowel of the rāʾ to the bāʾ, so that one does not need to produce part of the vowel in pausal form, nor to make it quiescent and thus join two quiescent letters. This is a widespread dialect, not an anomalous one but a well-attested one, and it indicates the case-ending and separation from the meeting of two quiescent letters, and its basis is that the pausal form should be quiescent. End of quote. We have cited in explanation of this, in the Sharh al-Tashil, several verses, such as the saying of the rajaz poet:

"I am Jarir, my kunya is Abu ʿAmr / I strike with the sword, and Saʿd is in the ʿAsr."

He means: Abu ʿAmr. And al-ʿAsr. And al-insan (mankind) is a generic noun that encompasses all, and for this reason the exception from it is valid. And al-khusr is loss (al-khusran), like kufr and kufran. And what loss is greater than that of one who loses both this world and the Hereafter? Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd ibn ʿAli, and Harun from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read ﴿khusur﴾ with a damma on the sin, while the majority read it with sukun. Whoever sells his Hereafter for his worldly life is in the utmost loss, unlike the believer, who has bought the Hereafter with the world, so he profits and is blessed.

﴿And enjoin one another to truth (al-ḥaqq)﴾: that is, to the established matter from those who act upon it and enjoin it upon one another. ﴿And enjoin one another to patience (al-ṣabr)﴾ in obedience to Allah the Exalted, and in abstaining from sins.
